ai.title: CLI feedback submits to new /api/v1/feedback endpoint
ai.summary: CLI feedback now posts to `web/src/app/api/v1/feedback` instead of relying on local-only state. `feedback-submission.ts` handles the network call, while `common/src/schemas/feedback.ts` validates the payload. `feedback-container.tsx` tracks `isSubmitting` to lock input during the request. Category types are now strictly enforced via `FeedbackCategory` from `common/src/constants/feedback.ts`.

eli5.text: When you submit feedback from the CLI now, it actually sends your feedback to the company's servers instead of just staying on your computer. The moment you hit submit, the input box locks up so you can't click it again while it's being sent. The system also makes sure you pick a valid category (like 'good result' or 'app bug') before submitting, rather than accepting any text you type. This is live today, and the developers noted that the server doesn't handle duplicate submissions yet, so don't spam the submit button.

ai.title: Fix Bedrock assistant prefill error in CLI agents
ai.summary: CLI agent definitions now send prefill context as user messages instead of assistant messages to resolve Bedrock API errors. The `create-cli-agent` helper explicitly excludes Amazon Bedrock from provider options. This change affects `claude-code-cli`, `codebuff-local-cli`, `codex-cli`, and `gemini-cli` definitions.

eli5.text: When the system runs certain AI coding tools on your behalf, it used to tell the tool it was already doing the work before actually handing off the task, which confused one of Amazon's AI services into rejecting the request. Now it frames those same instructions as something the tool should do next, so the handoff completes without error. If you watch the system start one of these coding tools, you'll see it set up a workspace session and then immediately begin working, just without the brief miscommunication that was causing retries.

ai.title: Handle empty tool result content in convertToolResultMessage
ai.summary: Added guard in `convertToolResultMessage` to handle empty `content` arrays by returning a single `tool-result` with empty JSON output. Prevents errors when processing tool messages with no content parts. Scope limited to `common/src/util/messages.ts`.

eli5.text: When a tool returns a result, the system now handles cases where that tool doesn't actually produce any content, instead of crashing or showing an error. This makes the experience more stable, especially when tools finish a task but don't have a specific message to pass back.

ai.title: Rename editor-glm to editor-lite and update to MiniMax M2.5
ai.summary: Renamed `editor-glm` to `editor-lite` and switched underlying models to `minimax/minimax-m2.5`. Updated `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts` to map `editor-lite`, `base2-free`, and `commander-lite` to MiniMax M2.5. Modified `agents/base2/base2.ts` prompts and `agents/editor/editor.ts` logic to reflect the new agent ID and model choice. Adjusted `web/src/content/tips/modes.mdx` to display MiniMax M2.5 in the Free mode documentation.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff in Free mode, your coding tasks now run on a different, presumably faster and cheaper AI model called MiniMax M2.5 instead of the previous GLM 4.7. The assistant that writes code changes has also been renamed from 'editor-glm' to 'editor-lite', and any documentation or in-app descriptions that mentioned the old name or old model now show the new ones. The switch is already in place for Free mode users today.

ai.title: Free tier drops editor-lite, adds code-reviewer-lite
ai.summary: Base2 free tier no longer spawns editor-lite; instead, the main agent implements changes directly via str_replace/write_file and spawns code-reviewer-lite. code-reviewer-lite is a new agent definition using minimax/minimax-m2.5. editor-lite model switched from glm to minimax, and editor.ts updated to accept 'minimax' instead of 'glm'.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of the service, instead of one assistant making code edits and then handing off to a separate editor assistant (now dropped), the main assistant writes the changes itself and brings in a new lightweight reviewer assistant to check the work. You would notice the extra review step appearing right after edits are made, and the free editor assistant that used to run on one AI provider is now running on a different one (MiniMax), while everything else about how you reach the free tier or its limits has not changed for existing users today.

ai.title: Docs update Free mode model to MiniMax M2.5
ai.summary: Documentation updates reflect Free mode switching from Grok 4.1 Fast to MiniMax M2.5. The Reviewer agent now lists MiniMax M2.5 for Free mode, and FAQ/advanced docs confirm this model handles Free mode editing and code review. Changes affect web/src/content/advanced/how-does-it-work.mdx, web/src/content/advanced/what-models.mdx, and web/src/content/help/faq.mdx.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff for free, the helper that checks your code for mistakes now runs on a different system called MiniMax M2.5 instead of the old one. The free helper also joins the main editing helper, so your free code reviews should look more consistent with the rest of what the tool does. The public docs and FAQ now tell you which system handles free work, replacing the old name everywhere it was mentioned.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 1.0.618
ai.summary: The CLI package manifest in cli/release/package.json was bumped from 1.0.617 to 1.0.618 as part of the standard release process. This version bundles the preceding day's fixes including abort-safe streaming in agent-runtime and SDK run, network-backed CLI feedback submission to /api/v1/feedback, Bedrock prefill-as-user-message handling, empty tool-result guards, the editor-glm to editor-lite rename with MiniMax M2.5, the Free tier swap to code-reviewer-lite, and Free mode documentation updates.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field incremented from 1.0.617 to 1.0.618, a +1/-1 diff in the version string only, marking a release-bump commit with no other file modifications.

eli5.text: This release upgrades the Freebuff CLI to version 1.0.618, switching Free mode editing and code review to the new MiniMax M2.5 model and retiring the old editor-lite agent in favor of a dedicated code-reviewer-light agent. Your feedback now gets sent directly through the app instead of staying on your machine, and canceling an in-progress task no longer risks losing the partial results already generated. The agent engine now flushes all buffered output before canceling, and the CLI handles Bedrock model quirks by sending setup context as regular messages. Upgrading gives you a more reliable Free mode powered by MiniMax M2.5, faster code reviews from the new reviewer agent, and the peace of mind that stopping a run mid-stream keeps your history intact.
